label: D2 step late in the episode (episode-clock unit; earlier ramp after choosing a1)
explanation: Reset-gate unit 0 fires almost only at D2 (97.5% of mass; never at GO, a little at D1) and only in the last ~20 trials of the 100-trial episode (zero activity before trial 70; rate 0.9% at 80-89, 27% at 90-99). So it works as an episode-end clock. It crosses threshold earlier when the trial chose a1 (in_action == 1 at D2, which is 79% of mass) than after a2, which only crosses near trials 90+. Magnitude grows with ep_trial: the top quartile is ~99% covered and the windows ramp up across successive late trials. The model value output is low on these steps (an episode-end correlate; value < 5.22 alone gives F1 0.67). It does not depend on reward, transition type, stay/switch or the good state. The simple predicate D2 & ep_trial >= 85 gives F1 0.72 / mass recall 0.94; the recorded action-dependent threshold reaches dev F1 0.82 / mass recall 0.96. It uses only observed variables (ep_trial is implicit time; the action is observed at D2).

issues: The factual claims check out. GO: 0 active steps (F1 0). D1: 2.5% of mass, 5% of active steps. D2: 97.5% of mass. No activity before trial 70. Active rate is 0.6% at trials 70-79, 9.1% at 80-89 and 27.1% at 90-99 (the label's 0.9% for trials 80-89 is a slight misstatement; the measured rate is 9.1%). a1 at D2 carries 79.5% of mass. The original predicate reproduces on test: P 0.741, R 0.908, F1 0.816, mass recall 0.96. D2 & ep_trial>=85 gives test F1 0.703. D2 & value<5.22 gives test F1 0.679.

The clock ramp is clean and the a1/a2 offset is systematic. For a1 at D2, precision is 0.37 at trials 80-84, 0.82 at 85-89, 0.99 at 90-94 and 1.0 at 95-99. For a2 at D2 it is 0.0 at 80-84, 0.02 at 85-89, 0.37 at 90-94 and 0.85 at 95-99.

Small overclaim: the explanation says the unit is independent of transition type. In fact the reached state (in_state) also shifts the onset by about 3 trials. In the a1, trials 80-87 boundary band, precision is 0.57 when S1 is reached and 0.35 when S2 is reached. The onset is earliest for a1->S1, then a1->S2, a2->S1, a2->S2. Reward and prev_reward have no effect (0.49 vs 0.57). The good state matters only through its correlation with the choice.

Misses (4% of mass) are mostly D1 steps in late a1 runs, where activity carries over from the previous D2. The weak low-quartile activations are scattered. The false positives sit at the onset boundary (trials 80-84 for a1), not in any separate class. Activations also seem to grow over runs of consecutive a1 choices, but conditioning on prev_action==1 does not raise precision (0.52 vs 0.45 in the boundary band). So that is part of the ramp, not a separate rule.
The predicate uses no future variables: in_action and in_state are both observed at D2, and ep_trial is elapsed time.
